assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-range electron transfer through proteins established, with kinetics on ruthenium-modified proteins and tunneling-pathway analysis, how electrons cross tens of angstroms through a protein medium. This is the physical basis of respiratory and photosynthetic energy conversion and directly informs how redox enzymes work. Mechanism is stated in physical terms and tested quantitatively.
assessment.attribution: Gray and Winkler are the decisive experimental and conceptual pair for protein electron-tunneling work. Marcus theory was already recognized in 1992, and related theory (Beratan, Onuchic, Dutton) lies outside the supplied credit, so the allocation is workable but the theory side needs care in the citation.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of independent confirmation, with the framework textbook-standard in bioinorganic and biophysical chemistry. Recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Overlap with theory and with Dutton's work not represented in the credited names could make the citation contested.
I cannot independently verify the full priority history from the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation turns small molecules into inducers of ubiquitin-mediated proteolysis. PROTACs and molecular glue degraders, with the cereblon mechanism of thalidomide, opened a new chemical modality that is now widely used in drug discovery and in the clinic. Conceptual originality and breadth of impact are high.
assessment.attribution: Credit is split between the PROTAC concept (Crews, Deshaies, Sakamoto), the glue mechanism (Handa, Ito) and later degrader chemistry (Ciulli, Gray). With eight names, three laureates must be chosen and the choice is contested. I propose Crews and Deshaies for the heterobifunctional concept and Handa for the cereblon mechanism.
assessment.maturity: Clinical trials of degraders are advanced but approvals are still pending. The mechanistic basis is well confirmed by structures and many groups.
uncertainties: Allocation between PROTAC and molecular-glue lines is unresolved.
Clinical validation is incomplete, so timing may be early for some committee members.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base to another without double-strand cleavage, a conceptually new use of engineered chemistry on DNA. The chemical design of deaminase-Cas fusions gave precision editing that is already used in therapeutic programs.
assessment.attribution: Liu is clearly the central figure and has the larger body of work (also prime editing). Komor and Gaudelli were first authors of the key studies and Nishida and Kondo reported an independent deaminase-based approach, so a two-to-three-person prize is possible. I propose Liu alone for clarity, as the single-laureate case is the cleanest.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced widely since 2016, and first clinical results exist. The Nobel went to CRISPR in 2020, so the committee may see base editing as a refinement; prize timing is uncertain.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as chemistry or as follow-on to the 2020 CRISPR prize.
Long-term clinical safety and efficacy are still unfolding.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer gives the physical framework for concerted movement of protons and electrons in enzymes, water oxidation and fuel-forming catalysis. It is directly relevant to proton-pumping and redox enzymes I know best, with theory and experiment meeting. Fundamental and broad.
assessment.attribution: Meyer (early PCET and water oxidation catalysts), Mayer (bond-weakening and PCET thermochemistry) and Hammes-Schiffer (theory of vibronic PCET) are distinct complementary contributions. Nocera is also strong, via the PCET-based artificial photosynthesis work, so the three-person limit forces a difficult choice.
assessment.maturity: Concepts are mature and widely adopted. Application to enzymes is partly interpretive, and the field is less a single discovery than a line of work.
uncertainties: Rests on a line of work rather than one discovery, which affects how clearly a citation can be written.
Priority among Meyer, Mayer and Nocera is debatable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The energy-landscape and funnel view resolved the Levinthal paradox in physical terms and gave a statistical-mechanical foundation for protein folding, with experiments from Fersht on transition states and phi-values. It brings physics to biological chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic are the main authors of landscape theory; Dill's hydrophobic-collapse view is an important alternative, and Fersht is the leading experimentalist. Bryngelson is credited but the three-laureate limit makes allocation hard.
assessment.maturity: Concepts have held for thirty years and are now embedded in structure prediction and design. Some predictive value was shown, but the deeper triumph of structure prediction came by machine learning (2024 prize).
uncertainties: The 2024 prize for protein structure prediction and design may reduce the appetite for another protein-folding award.
Allocation between theory and experiment is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase structure and mechanism clarify how biological nitrogen fixation works through the FeMo-cofactor, including the interstitial carbide and the electron and proton delivery that drives N2 reduction. This is a fundamental metalloenzyme mechanism.
assessment.attribution: Rees led the first structures and the cofactor characterization, Einsle resolved the central atom, and Dean (with Seefeldt, Ribbe) established the genetics and biochemistry. The credited set is plausible but contested.
assessment.maturity: Structures are confirmed in several labs. The reduction mechanism at the atomic level is still debated, so the final picture is not yet stable.
uncertainties: The catalytic mechanism of N2 reduction is not fully settled.
Credit between structural and biochemical contributors is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography uses X-ray free-electron laser pulses to collect diffraction before damage, giving room-temperature structures and time-resolved views of reactions in proteins. It makes dynamic mechanisms visible, as I value.
assessment.attribution: Chapman made the foundational diffraction-before-destruction demonstration and Fromme and Schlichting contributed protein crystallography and time-resolved studies. Hajdu is also credited, but I am uncertain about his current status, so I did not rely on him.
assessment.maturity: The method is established, but the science returns on time-resolved mechanisms are still coming. Number of landmark findings is limited relative to its promise.
uncertainties: Whether method maturity is sufficient for recognition.
Credit among many contributors to XFEL development is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multidimensional solution NMR methods from isotope labeling and triple-resonance experiments to relaxation dispersion and TROSY-based approaches for large proteins gave atomic-level structure and dynamics of biomolecules in solution. Dynamic mechanisms become measurable.
assessment.attribution: Bax, Clore and Kay made the most influential methodological advances in these areas, though Wüthrich was already recognized in 2002 and the line from Palmer and Wagner is also relevant. The three proposed names are defensible but not unique.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with decades of broad use. Recognition would be late, and the committee must be mindful that NMR has been awarded several times.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier NMR prizes may lower priority.
Rests on a family of methods rather than one discovery.
